subject: mathematics
question_text: For what value of λ are the vectors i − λj + 2k and 8i + 6j − k at right angles?

mark_split.label: State the condition for right angles

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.73, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 26(ii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives one mark each to the condition, the dot product, the solving and the check. NOTE ON LENGTH: the book files this under Short Answer, so the card carries the 4 marks a Maths-1A Section B question is worth (PAPER_PATTERNS holds every SAQ to 4). The mathematics is one line of dot product, so the fourth mark is given to the substitution check rather than to invented working. This is a DOT-product question, not a scalar-triple-product one, although it sits among the box-product items in this section. Checked: with λ = 1, (1)(8) + (−1)(6) + (2)(−1) = 8 − 6 − 2 = 0 exactly. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find λ — the condition for right angles, the dot product, and the check at the end.

steps.label: State the condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Dot product zero is perpendicular; cross product zero is parallel. Do not swap them.
steps.memory_tip: Dot is zero for perpendicular, cross is zero for parallel.
lines: Let a = i − λj + 2k and b = 8i + 6j − k.
Two non-zero vectors are at right angles

recall.must_convey: That two non-zero vectors are at right angles exactly when their dot product is zero.
accept: at right angles means the dot product is zero
set a dot b equal to zero
perpendicular vectors have zero dot product
perpendicular ante dot product zero
the condition is a dot b equals zero
reject: eight minus six lambda minus two

steps.why: a·b = |a||b|cos θ, and neither length is zero here, so the product vanishes only when cos θ = 0, that is θ = 90°.
common_mistakes: Using a × b = 0, which is the condition for parallel vectors.

steps.label: Write the dot product
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Match i with i, j with j, k with k. The signs of the components travel with them.
steps.memory_tip: Three products, one per axis, then add. Nothing crosses between axes.

recall.must_convey: That the dot product is 8 − 6λ − 2, that is 6 − 6λ.
accept: one times eight, minus lambda times six, two times minus one
the dot product is eight minus six lambda minus two
that simplifies to six minus six lambda
dot product six minus six lambda avthundi
multiply matching components and add
reject: set the dot product to zero

steps.why: The dot product multiplies matching components and adds them, so each of the three coordinate pairs contributes one term.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus that travels with the −λ component.
Multiplying the i part of one vector by the j part of the other.

steps.label: Solve for λ
steps.margin_note: Third mark. A single linear equation, so a single answer.
steps.memory_tip: 6 − 6λ = 0 means 6λ = 6, so λ = 1. Move the term across before dividing.

accept: six minus six lambda is zero so six lambda is six
lambda equals one
move the term across and divide by six
six lambda six, so lambda one
solve the linear equation for lambda
reject: the dot product is six minus six lambda

steps.why: The equation is linear in λ, so there is exactly one value that makes the two vectors perpendicular.

steps.label: Check by substitution
steps.margin_note: Last mark. One line of arithmetic proves the answer; the check is worth writing out.
steps.memory_tip: 8 − 6 − 2 = 0. Write the check; it costs one line and proves the answer.

recall.must_convey: That substituting λ = 1 gives a dot product of exactly zero.
accept: put lambda equals one back and the dot product is eight minus six minus two
that is zero, so the vectors are perpendicular
the check confirms lambda is one
lambda one pettina dot product zero vasthundi
substitute and verify the dot product is zero

steps.why: Substituting the value back shows the dot product really is zero, so the two vectors really are at right angles.
common_mistakes: Giving λ = 1 with no check line.
Checking with the original −λj instead of −j.
